verified.exploit_entry_point: A raw HTTP request carrying an Authorization credential, driven through the project's own LocalConnector against a real SecurityHandler-protected path: (a) a Digest challenge/response handled by the core security handler, with the account's plain secret in a UserStore; (b) the same challenge/response in the servlet-environment security handler (jetty-ee9-security); (c) HTTP Basic against a stored, pre-computed password digest (MD5: or SHA256:); (d) HTTP Basic against a stored credential minted from the account's real secret by the server's own password-preparation path (Credential.MD5.digest, the producer used by the command-line password utility), which encodes with the same legacy charset, so the stored bytes themselves are lossy and a wrong value that collapses onto them authenticates even after every checking method is fixed. In every case a response computed from a different secret that maps to the same legacy bytes authenticates on the pinned+injected code (HTTP 200 and the user marker) and is refused (a 4xx client error, no marker) after the fix. Digest responses are computed by the test itself from the nonce advertised in the challenge, so no product code computes the asserted value; only the producer route uses product code, to mint the account's stored secret exactly as an administrator's tool would.
sites: core DigestAuthenticator.Digest.check: H(A1) = user:realm:password encoded with ISO-8859-1 (reported site; the default MD5 branch)
core DigestAuthenticator.Digest.check: the injected SHA-256 algorithm branch computes its own H(A1) with the same legacy encoding (injected sibling S1)
jetty-ee9-security DigestAuthenticator.Digest.check: the servlet-environment copy of the same decision (far site, second implementation)
Credential.MD5.check: a stored MD5: credential hashes the submitted password with ISO-8859-1 (pattern B, reached by HTTP Basic with charset=UTF-8); Credential.MD5.digest is the matching producer
Credential.SHA256.check: the injected SHA256: stored-credential type hashes with the same legacy encoding (injected sibling S2); Credential.SHA256.digest is the matching producer

Credential.MD5.digest: the real upstream producer the check never calls; the command-line password utility mints a stored MD5: credential by hashing the configured secret with ISO-8859-1, so the stored value is lossy before any checking method runs (how-type lever M6)
verified.uncovered_routes_pattern_B: Credential.MD5.check is real, unmodified upstream code (present in latest) and is reached from a real request path (Basic/Form login against an MD5: property-store credential). It is registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv and is built into the task. Its matching producer Credential.MD5.digest is also real: the command-line password utility uses it to mint stored credentials, and the producer route built here mints the account's stored value with it and then authenticates over HTTP Basic, so it is now built as a how-type (M6) lever rather than dismissed. The jetty-client DigestAuthentication lossy encoding is a far site that only ever affects the client's own hashing, so it cannot express a server-side attack and is dismissed (not built).
injected_siblings: S1 core DigestAuthenticator: a configurable digest algorithm (setAlgorithm/getAlgorithm) with a SHA-256 response branch; the challenge advertises the configured value, the parser accepts an algorithm parameter, and the branch hashes A1 with ISO-8859-1. A maintainer adding RFC 7616 SHA-256 support next to the existing MD5 path could plausibly write exactly this.

S2 core Credential: a SHA256: stored-credential type next to MD5:/CRYPT:, selected by Credential.getCredential and checked with MESSAGE-DIGEST over ISO-8859-1 bytes; a modern hashed-password format a maintainer could plausibly add.
verified.project_tests_run: During the image build (online) the project's own BasicAuthenticatorTest (core) and the servlet environment's ConstraintTest#testDigest are compiled and run against the pinned+injected tree; both pass. Hidden suite: 7 security + 11 functional JUnit cases across two modules; on the pinned+injected tree all 7 security fail and all 11 functional pass, and on the oracle all 18 pass, offline.
